artworks.title: This Other Eden: Photographs by Anne Rearick
artworks.description: Opens Nov 14, 2026. Through more than 60 photographs taken at Gloucester’s Stage Fort Park, documentary photographer Anne Rearick captures the gatherings, traditions, and quiet moments that bring people together. From family picnics to weddings and baptisms, her images reveal the park as a place of respite, connection, and shared experience. A Guggenheim Fellowship recipient and longtime Gloucester resident, Rearick invites viewers to consider themes of belonging, community, and the importance of shared public spaces. An adjacent gallery explores the history of Stage Fort Park, which has been open to the public since 1898. The exhibition is accompanied by a fully illustrated catalog featuring essays by Rearick,

artworks.title: 150 Years and Beyond: Highlights from the Library & Archives
artworks.description: Opens Nov 14, 2026. .av-layout-tab.av-ltpssy-0f5027e25469275ded893594c7189f21{ vertical-align:middle; } In 1875 – 150 years ago – the Cape Ann Scientific and Literary Association was founded. The next century and a half saw the growth of CAM’s archival holdings, with strengths in documenting Cape Ann’s culture and history, including the fisheries industry, local artists and art colonies, and writers and illustrators. Composed almost entirely of material from the Cape Ann Museum’s Library & Archives, this exhibit highlights the varied stories of Cape Ann as told through material in the Library & Archives. #top .hr.hr-invisible.av-2ao8w3-7bb065717f233e3da4a8e67f2a5dca12{ height:25px; }
